_about: The faith hub (plan 7.6f), the third built after love and righteousness, and the one the review panel flagged high (ontology/provenance/concept-hubs/committee-flags.json): whether the Greek πίστις and the Hebrew אֱמוּנָה mean belief or faithfulness, whether 'faith of Christ' is faith in him or his own faithfulness, and how faith stands to works, to the law, to grace and to baptism. The rows are defined by the Hebrew and Greek as in the other two hubs (a noun row by the words in the noun's own phrase or verse, a verb row by the verb's clause, a pick row by hand). Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/faith.json. 26 rows (13 noun, 10 verb, 3 adjective); what no row takes is listed under 'More' in each form.

titles.noun: What the text says of faith

_words_why: The family in both testaments: πίστις (noun), πιστεύω (verb), πιστός (adjective) and ὀλιγόπιστος 'of little faith'; and the Hebrew אָמַן (believe, trust; in its passive 'be faithful'), אֱמוּנָה and אֱמוּן (faithfulness). Hebrew and Greek are listed together because the text puts them side by side (Gen 15:6 and Rom 4:3), but the hub never says they are one word: the Hebrew nouns have their own row, the Greek noun's 'faithfulness' verses have theirs. The negations ἀπιστία, ἄπιστος, ἀπιστέω are not in the family: the card 'unbelief' is a door, and they are named in 'Other words' because the English also calls them 'unbelief'.
_sense_why: Measured on MACULA's gloss in each verse (2026-10-10). What the gloss says decides, and the hub says so on the row. πίστις: 'faith' in 226 of 227 verses; 'faithfulness' (Rom 3:3, Gal 5:22, Matt 23:23) and 'fidelity' (Titus 2:10) are kept, and set in their own row rather than counted as faith. Acts 17:31 'a guarantee' (proof, not faith) falls out. πιστεύω: 'believe' for 208 verses; 'entrusted with' (1 Cor 9:17, Gal 2:7, 1 Tim 1:11, Titus 1:3, Rom 3:2, Luke 16:11, John 2:24, 1 Thess 2:4) falls out as another sense, and Acts 13:39 (gloss is the Greek itself, 'πιστεύων') falls out of the machinery but is put back by hand in the row that names it. אָמַן: 99 verses, 'be firm, confirmed, nurse, guardians' fall out (33 verses), 'believe', 'trust' and the passive 'faithful', 'trustworthy' stay. אֱמוּנָה: 'faithfulness', 'faith' (Hab 2:4), 'trust' (1 Chr 9:22, 9:26: a position of trust) stay; 'truth', 'integrity', 'honesty', 'steady', 'stability' fall out. The words 'unfaithful' and 'unbelief' do not match: a leading 'un' leaves no word boundary, so the negations are not counted as the concept.

others._why: Other words the English also calls faith, believing or trusting, kept apart as love keeps φιλέω and חֶסֶד apart. בָּטַח (trust, 117 uses in the family of 'put confidence in') is the Old Testament's other commonest word for it and is NOT אָמַן; חָסִיד and אֱמֶת are 'faithful' and 'truth'. 'unbelie...' is left out of the pattern: the negations have their own card.
others.title: Other words translated “faith”, “believe”, “trust”

_own_words_why: Rom 3:28 and Jas 2:24 stand side by side on purpose; Hab 2:4 and Gen 15:6 are the two Old Testament verses the New Testament leans on.

Hos.12.1.why: the Hebrew's 12:1 holds 'faithful to the Holy One' (the Hebrew counts Hos 12:1 as the Berean's 11:12); the Berean prints those words in 11:12, so 12:1 as shown has no 'faithful'

_review: Written against the panel's note (committee-flags.json, 'faith', worry high): keep each phrase as the Berean reads it with 'faith in Christ' and 'faithfulness of Christ' not resolved; place the Pauline 'by faith' rows and the James 'faith without deeds' rows side by side; give the noun and the verb as separate forms and do not state they are the same thing. match 'all' so a verse that names faith and works stands in both rows, and no row's order decides Jas 2:24 or Rom 3:28. The Greek companion rows test Greek lemmas only, so a Hebrew 'faithfulness' verse never lands under a row that says 'faith'.
_consolidation: 2026-10-10, at the coordinator's request (brief rule 8: about 15-25 rows, never 40+): the first build had 68 rows, a concordance. Merged: the three preposition rows (διά, ἐκ, the dative alone) into one; circumcision into the law row; 'credited as righteousness' into the justified row (its three verses were already in it by rule); grace and 'When Jesus saw their faith' into the saved row; baptism, repentance and the Spirit's rows into one; love, hope, endurance, obedience into one; hearing, the word, doubt, little/great faith and growing/failing into one; the Hebrew 'beside loving devotion', 'beside righteousness' and 'The LORD's faithfulness' into the one Hebrew row (they were subsets of it); the verb rows believe-that, believe-what-is-said and believing-a-person into one; seeing, hearing, asking, speaking, saved and eternal life into one; 'Him' and 'the Lord' into one no-choice row; works and justified into one verb row; baptized, repent and the Spirit into one; the adjective rows into three. Dropped without a row of their own (their verses are in a broader row or under 'More'): 'Faith and what is not seen' (5; all five stand in the phrase or company row), the shield and breastplate of faith (2; 1 Thess 5:8 is in the company row, Eph 6:16 under More), 'Faith and prayer' (6; five of them stand in other rows, 2 Thess 1:11 in works). The catch-all rows ('Every other use') were dropped too: the builder already lists what no row takes under 'More', so they added a row and no verse. Not merged, on purpose: the gloss split, 'faith in Christ / faithfulness of Christ', the faith/works/law/justified rows, the baptism row in both forms, the God, Jesus and 'Him / the Lord / He is faithful' rows, 'The faith', the Hebrew verb as 'faithful'.

rows.label: Where the gloss for πίστις is “faithfulness”, not “faith”
rows.note: The same Greek word. In these verses the gloss for it is “faithfulness” or “fidelity”; in the rest of this list it is “faith”. The page lets the gloss decide, does not say that faith and faithfulness are one meaning, and does not say which meaning a verse carries where the gloss reads “faith”. Titus 2:10 reads “good faith” in the Berean.
rows._why: The panel's first worry. Rom 3:3 (the faithfulness of God), Gal 5:22 (the Spirit's fruit), Matt 23:23 (justice, mercy and faithfulness) and Titus 2:10 are the four verses where MACULA's gloss for g4102 is not 'faith'. By hand because the builder cannot condition a row on the gloss. Matt 23:23 and Gal 5:22 are kept out of the law, love and endurance rows for the same reason (not_verses); Rom 3:3 stands also under 'Faith beside God' and 'doubted', where its other words are.

rows.label: The Hebrew noun: “faithfulness” (אֱמוּנָה, אֱמוּן)
rows.note: Shown apart from the Greek πίστις: the Hebrew is not the Greek word. In the Psalms, Deuteronomy and Lamentations it is often the LORD's faithfulness (Ps 36:5, 89:1, Lam 3:23, Deut 32:4), and in Proverbs a person's (Prov 28:20). The Berean reads it “faithfulness” in nearly all of these verses and “faith” in one, Hab 2:4, which is quoted at Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:38. In a few verses the Berean's English is another word (“honest”, “trustworthy”, “entrusted”, a position of “trust”: Prov 14:5, 20:6; Ps 33:4; 1 Chr 9:22, 9:26); the Hebrew word is the one this row names.
rows._why: Panel: 'πίστις and אֱמוּנָה can mean either, let the gloss decide'. The Greek-only rows never take a Hebrew verse. It was four rows: all 43, 'The LORD's faithfulness' (22, by hand), beside loving devotion (12) and beside righteousness (10); the last three were subsets of the first. Panel fix (2026-10-10): second in the noun form, straight after the gloss row, not last; led by the Psalms, Lamentations and Deuteronomy, with Hab 2:4 inside the row and introduced after, not as the first example. A pick row now (the same 43 as the rule gave) because Deut 32:20 (h529, 'children of unfaithfulness', filed by MACULA outside the clause the rule reads) is added by hand.

rows.label: Through faith, by faith, from faith, of faith (διά, ἐκ, and the dative alone)
rows._why: Was three rows (διά 19, ἐκ 20, the dative 23); one list of 60 verses now, by hand from those three lists. The panel named διά and ἐκ and the Pauline 'by faith' with the ancients' 'by faith': the phrases are kept as the Berean reads them ('through', 'by', 'of', 'from') and say nothing about what they mean. In: the verses where Greek διά or ἐκ stands the very next word beside πίστις (Gal 5:6 is out: 'faith expressing itself through love' puts διά before love), and the dative πίστει with no preposition (the gloss 'By faith' in Heb 11:3-31, Rom 3:28, 11:20, Acts 26:18; Acts 15:9 and 2 Cor 1:24 are the same dative with the Berean's 'by faith'). Rom 3:25 is here by διά ('through faith'), not by ἐκ: MACULA files the ἐκ clause of 3:26 under 3:25. Gal 3:7 and 3:9 ('those who have faith') are the Greek 'those of faith' (ἐκ πίστεως), which the Berean smooths.

rows.label: Faith beside “Jesus” or “Christ”
rows.note: In Rom 3:22, 3:26, Gal 2:16, 2:20, 3:22, Phil 3:9, Jas 2:1 and Rev 14:12 the Greek puts the name in the genitive (“faith of Jesus Christ”); the Berean's “faith in” there is its reading of the phrase, and Rev 14:12 reads “the faith of Jesus”. Elsewhere (Col 1:4, 2:5, Eph 1:15, Acts 24:24) the Greek has a preposition meaning “in”. Readers part on the first group, on whether it means faith in Christ or Christ's own faithfulness; the page does not choose.
rows._why: The panel: do not resolve 'faith in Christ' against 'the faithfulness of Christ'. By hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names Jesus, Christ or the Son beside the noun, or is Jesus' own 'faith in Me' (Acts 26:18). Built from a window of three words either side of the noun (faith, in, Christ); the rule put Rom 3:25 here by the clause filing (its words are in 3:26) and missed 'faith and love that are in Christ Jesus' (1 Tim 1:14, 2 Tim 1:13), which are added. Panel fix (2026-10-10): the note names which verses are the Greek genitive and which have a preposition, and the leads show both (Rev 14:12 'the faith of Jesus', Col 1:4 'faith in Christ Jesus'); Eph 3:17 ('Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith') is neither 'faith in' nor 'faith of' and is out of this row (it stays in 'Through faith ...').

rows.label: Faith beside “God”
rows.note: The text's own phrases, kept as written (“faith in God”, “the faithfulness of God”); where readers part on whose faith or faithfulness a phrase names, the page does not choose.
rows._why: By hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names God beside the noun. A window rule on θεός and κύριος missed 1 Thess 1:8 and 1 Pet 1:21 and took 1 Tim 1:4 ('stewardship of God'), Titus 1:1 ('God's elect') and Rom 3:22 ('righteousness of God'), where 'God' belongs to the word beside it. Greek only: a Hebrew 'faithfulness of the LORD' never lands under 'faith'. 'The Lord' is not here: Eph 4:5 says 'one Lord, one faith' and the page does not say which person.

rows.label: Faith and works
rows.note: Set side by side with the rows on the law and on being justified, as the text has them: a verse that names both stands in each row it fits. Where Christian traditions part on how faith and works stand to each other (Rom 3:28; Jas 2:24), the page takes no side.
rows._why: The panel: put the Pauline 'by faith' beside James on works in one list. The rule is the Greek words for work and working in the verse; Gal 6:10 ('let us work good') and Heb 11:33 ('worked righteousness') are included because the Greek verb is there although the Berean's English does not say 'work'. The English 'deeds' of James (Jas 2:14-26) is the same Greek ἔργον.

rows.label: Faith and the law, the commandments, circumcision

not_verses.Matt.23.23: the gloss here is “faithfulness”, not “faith”; it stands in the first row and is not set under a row that says “faith”

rows.note: Set side by side with the rows on works and on being justified; a verse that names more than one stands in each. Matt 23:23 (the law: justice, mercy and faithfulness) is under “faithfulness”, where the gloss puts it.
rows._why: Circumcision (Gal 5:6, Rom 3:30, 4:9, 4:11, 4:12) was its own row of five; it is the same argument as the law in Paul and is joined here.

rows.label: Faith and righteousness: being justified, being credited
rows.note: Where Christian traditions part on what it is to be justified by faith, and how works stand to it, the page takes no side. A verse that names works as well stands in the row for works.
rows._why: Mirrors the righteousness hub's 'Righteousness and faith'. Rom 4:5, 4:9 and 4:11 ('credited as righteousness') were their own row of three; each already contains δικαιοσύνη, so the rule takes them. 1 Tim 6:11 and 2 Tim 2:22 ('pursue righteousness, faith, love') are the same words in a list, not 'justified by faith'; the label says 'and'.

rows.label: Faith with being saved, made well or forgiven, and with grace

not_verses.1Tim.1.2: 'Grace, mercy, and peace' is the letter's greeting; 'faith' is in the address
not_verses.1Tim.6.21: 'Grace be with you all' is the letter's closing; 'the faith' is in the clause before
not_verses.Titus.3.15: 'Grace be with all of you' is the letter's closing; 'in the faith' is in the clause before

rows.note: The Greek verb σῴζω is “saved” in some verses and “healed” or “made well” in others (“your faith has healed you”); the page does not say which is meant where the English chose. Where Christian traditions part on how grace, faith and works stand to each other (Eph 2:8-10, where 2:9 reads “not by works” and 2:10 “created in Christ Jesus to do good works”; Rom 4:16; Jas 2:14), the page takes no side.
rows._why: Was three rows: saved/made well (19), grace (8) and 'When Jesus saw their faith' (Matt 9:2, Mark 2:5, Luke 5:20: in each the paralytic is told his sins are forgiven; added by hand). One Greek verb, two English renderings (rule 6): Luke 7:50 'Your faith has saved you' and Luke 8:48 'Your faith has healed you' are both σέσωκέν σε. Grace is flagged medium by the panel; Eph 2:9 itself holds no faith word, so it is named in the note, not in the row.

rows.label: Faith with repentance, baptism and the Spirit
rows.note: A verse stands here only where faith and baptism, repentance or the Spirit are in the same verse; verses side by side in the text (Gal 3:26 and 3:27) are not joined. Where Christian traditions part on how baptism, repentance and the Spirit stand to faith, the page takes no side.
rows._why: Was four rows: baptism (Col 2:12, Eph 4:5), repentance (Acts 20:21, Heb 6:1), the Holy Spirit (8) and the Spirit's fruit and gifts (Gal 5:22, 1 Cor 12:9). By hand (divine persons by hand): each Spirit verse names the Spirit; the rule on πνεῦμα also took a man's spirit (Jas 2:26, Col 2:5, Phil 1:27). The builder has no 'this verse or the next' condition, so Gal 3:26-27 and Acts 16:31-33 are named in the note and not shown. Not hidden, not joined. Panel fix (2026-10-10): Gal 5:22 (gloss 'faithfulness') was in this row under a 'faith' label and is out, it stands in the first row; the label now names repentance first (the order of Mark 1:15, Acts 20:21, Heb 6:1) and the leads open with Gal 3:2, Acts 20:21, Col 2:12, Eph 4:5 because only two of the 13 verses name baptism and the rest are about the Spirit.

rows.label: Faith with love, hope, endurance and obedience

not_verses.Gal.5.22: the gloss here is “faithfulness”, not “faith”; it stands in the first row
not_verses.Luke.17.6: ὑπακούω here is the tree obeying ('it would obey you')
not_verses.Luke.8.25: ὑπακούω here is the winds and the waves obeying

rows._why: Was five rows: love (23), hope (9), endurance and testing (14), obedience (4) and the shield and breastplate of faith (1 Thess 5:8 stands here by love and hope; Eph 6:16 is under More). What the text sets in the same verse as faith, in lists ('faith, hope and love', 'faith and patience') and in the 'obedience that comes from faith' (Rom 1:5, 16:26).

rows.label: Faith with hearing, the word, doubt, and “little” and “great” faith
rows.note: Where the text speaks of faith as heard (Rom 10:17), as given (Rom 12:3, Eph 2:8) or as granted (Phil 1:29), see the other rows; the page does not say which comes first.
rows._why: Was five rows: hearing (Rom 10:17, Gal 3:2, 3:5, Heb 4:2), the word and the gospel (11), doubt and unbelief (7), little faith, great faith, the mustard seed (7) and faith that grows or fails (11); by hand now so the whole row is one list. Hearing is ἀκοή only: ἀκούω pulled in 'When Jesus heard this' (Matt 8:10). 'Great faith' (Matt 8:10, 15:28, Luke 7:9) and 'move a mountain' (Matt 21:21, 1 Cor 13:2) are by hand: the English word 'great' is too common for a rule. Acts 15:9 (διακρίνω 'make a distinction') is not here. 1 Thess 3:10 ('supply what is lacking in your faith') was in the prayer row.

rows.label: “The faith”: held, kept, shared, fought for, left
rows.note: Where the text speaks of “the faith” as something held, kept, contended for or left, readers part on whether it means what is believed or the believing itself; the page does not choose.
rows._why: By hand: the rule on verbs (keep, deny, abandon, fight) took Heb 11:24 ('refused to be called') and missed Acts 6:7, Gal 1:23 and the 'stand firm' verses. The 26 are those where the noun is the object of keeping, standing in, contending for or leaving. Titus 1:4 ('our common faith') is the 27th (panel 'missing': MACULA files its clause outside what the builder reads, so no rule reached it); it is placed here, with 'shared' added to the label, because 'the faith' held in common is the nearest of the rows to what the verse says.

rows.label: Believe the LORD, believe in God
rows.note: Rom 4:24 and John 5:24 name God by what He did: “Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead”, “Him who sent Me”.
rows._why_added: Rom 4:24 and John 5:24 added on Doug's decision, 2026-10-10 (the panel's proposal): the text names the one believed by what He did, not by a title; the note says so
rows._why: By hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names God or the LORD as the one believed. Hebrew and Greek in one row because the text itself sets Gen 15:6 under Rom 4:3 and Gal 3:6; the row does not say אָמַן and πιστεύω are one word. John 14:1 is also in the row for Jesus: 'believe in God; believe in Me as well'. Rom 15:13 is not here: the Greek does not name God in the clause. (Rom 4:24 was left out on the same ground until Doug's decision; see _why_added.)

rows.label: Believe in Jesus, in the Son, in His name
rows._why: By hand (divine persons by hand). Each verse either names Jesus, Christ or the Son, or is Jesus' own 'in Me' ('believes in Me', Matt 18:6, John 11:25). 17 of these 36 are participles ('whoever believes in Him') that the frames do not carry, so a rule row would have lost John 3:16, 3:36, 6:40, 11:25, 1 John 5:1. Rom 3:22 and Gal 3:22 ('to all who believe') are in 'Those who believe': the verb has no object there.

rows.label: Believe in “Him”, “the One”, “the Lord”
rows.note: The text says “Him”, “the One” or “the Lord”, or describes him (“Him who sent Me”, “Him who raised Jesus”); where the verse does not name the person, the page does not choose.
rows._why: Panel fix (2026-10-10): the note was 'The text says only ...', which Rom 4:24, John 5:24 and 6:29 (descriptions the verse supplies) show to be overstated; reworded. Isa 28:16 left the row: the Hebrew verb has no object there ('the one who believes'), it is in 'Those who believe', and Rom 9:33 and 1 Pet 2:6 (which add 'in Him') stay here. Rom 4:24 and John 5:24 are not moved into the God row: that is Doug's per-record decision. Was two rows ('Him', 'the One' 17; 'the Lord' 6), joined under one note. Same rule as righteousness's “He is righteous”: where the text says only a pronoun, a description or 'the Lord', it is left unattributed. John 6:29 ('the One He has sent') and 5:24 ('Him who sent Me') are descriptions, not names. Acts 11:17 and 16:31 name 'the Lord Jesus' and are in the Jesus row.

rows.label: Believe a person, believe what is said, believe that …
rows._why: Was three rows: believe that (27), believe what is said, written, reported (25) and believing or trusting a person (25). By hand: the rule on 'that' (ὅτι) also took 'because' (John 4:39, 8:45, 10:26). Jas 2:19 (the demons believe that God is one) is the verse the panel will read beside Jas 2:24. 2 Thess 2:11 'believe the lie' and Prov 14:15 'believes every word' are here on purpose: the verb takes what is said, true or not. 'Take him at his word' (Gen 45:26, Judg 11:20, 1 Sam 27:12) shows that the verb is also ordinary human trust, not only a religious act.

rows.label: Not believing: “did not believe”, “do not believe”, “would not trust”
rows._why: Made from the builder's rule on a negative in the verb's own clause (62 verses) and then by hand, because the frames lack Jude 5 and the rule took 'we now believe not only because of your words' (John 4:42), 'though you have not seen Him' (1 Pet 1:8), 'not by works of the law' (Gal 2:16), 'unless you believed in vain' (1 Cor 15:2), 'does not believe in Me alone' (John 12:44), 'Believe Me that I am in the Father' (John 14:11), and Ps 78:8 and 78:37, where the Hebrew passive is 'faithful' and is in its own row. Job 15:22 is the Hebrew 'he does not believe he will return'; the Berean reads it 'despairs of his return', so the English does not show the label and the verse stays under 'More'.

rows.label: Believing with seeing, hearing, asking and speaking, and with being saved and living
rows.note: The Greek verb σῴζω is “saved” in some verses and “healed” or “made well” in others (Luke 8:50); the page does not say which is meant where the English chose. Mark 16:16 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack.
rows._why: Was six rows: seeing (13), hearing (15, a rule on ἀκούω), asking in prayer (4), speaking (5), saved (12), eternal life (12); by hand now so the whole row is one list. What the text sets in the same verse as believing. Taken out of the hearing rule: John 9:35 (Jesus heard the news), John 11:42 (He hears the prayer), Luke 8:50 (He overheard a report). Matt 27:42 ('He saved others ... we will believe') is the crowd's taunt and is in the 'Him' row. Acts 13:48 ('all who were appointed for eternal life believed') is in on purpose: every verse that names believing with eternal life or life is here, so no reader can say the row was chosen to avoid it; the page takes no side on what it implies.

rows.label: Believing with baptism, repentance and the Spirit
rows.note: A verse stands here only where believing and baptism, repentance or the Spirit are in the same verse; verses side by side in the text (Acts 16:31 and 16:33, believing and baptized in the jailer's household) are not joined. Mark 16:16 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack. Where Christian traditions part on how baptism, repentance and the Spirit stand to believing, the page takes no side.
rows._why: Was three rows: believe and be baptized (5), believe and repent (Mark 1:15, Matt 21:32) and believing and the Spirit (John 7:39, Eph 1:13, Acts 19:2). Mark 16:16 is in the passage the site marks everywhere it is shown; here it is named in the row's own note as well. Panel fix (2026-10-10): the old label 'Believe, and be baptized, repent, receive the Spirit' read as an imperative sequence (Mark 16:16's order, the reverse of Mark 1:15); it is now a 'with' list like the noun row, the leads no longer open with Mark 16:16 or Acts 19:2, and the note names Acts 16:31-33.

rows.label: Believing and works; believing, credited as righteousness, justified
rows.note: Set beside “Faith and works” and “Faith and righteousness” in the first list. The works here are the works of the law, the works of Jesus and good deeds; “credited” and “justified” are the text's own words. Where Christian traditions part on how faith and works stand to each other, or on what “credited” and “justified” mean, the page takes no side.
rows._why: Was two rows, works (12) and credited or justified (11), with Gal 2:16 and Rom 4:5 in both. By hand: the frames lack the participles John 14:12 ('whoever believes in Me will also do the works'), Rom 4:5 and Rom 4:11. Acts 13:39's gloss is the Greek itself ('πιστεύων'), so the sense test drops it; it is put back by hand because 'everyone who believes is justified' is exactly this row. Heb 4:3 ('works finished since the foundation') has the word in a different clause and is out.

rows.label: Those who believe: “believers”
rows._why: Rom 3:22 and Gal 3:22 ('to all who believe', 'to those who believe') were in the row for Jesus until the 16-verse check: the verb there has no object, the noun beside it is 'faith in Jesus Christ' and is in the noun form's row.

rows.label: The Hebrew verb as “faithful”, “trustworthy”
rows.note: The same Hebrew verb אָמַן that is “believe” and “trust” above. Where the gloss for it is “faithful” or “trustworthy” (the passive), the page lets the gloss decide and does not say that believing and being faithful are one meaning.
rows._why: The panel: let the gloss decide, and say so. The builder cannot condition a row on the gloss, so this row is by hand: the 20 verses where MACULA's gloss for אָמַן is 'faithful', 'trustworthy' or 'trusted'. Isa 55:3 (gloss 'faithful'; the Berean's 'My loving devotion promised to David') does not show the word and stays under 'More'. Hos 12:1 is the Berean's 11:12 (moves).

rows.label: “God is faithful”
rows._why: By hand: each names God (1 Pet 4:19 'a faithful Creator'). The same adjective is also 'believing'; the gloss, not the Greek word, divides these rows.

rows.label: “The Lord is faithful”, “He is faithful”, “Faithful and True”, the faithful witness
rows.note: Rev 1:5 names Jesus Christ. Heb 2:17 and 3:2 speak of the high priest whom Heb 3:1 calls Jesus; Heb 11:11, of the one who had promised. The rest say “the Lord”, “He”, “the One who calls you”, a witness, one called “Faithful and True”; readers take them of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: Was three rows ('The Lord is faithful' 6, 'Jesus Christ the faithful witness' Rev 1:5, 'Faithful and True: the high priest, the witness, the rider' 4), joined under the one no-choice note. Panel fix (2026-10-10): the note had put a settled attribution (Heb 2:17 and 3:2 are about Jesus by the book's own words, Heb 2:9 and 3:1; Heb 11:11 is the one who had promised) and an open one under one 'the page does not choose', which made the settled ones look contested; it now says which is which. The verses are not moved: Heb 11:11 does not name God, and the God row is by hand.

rows.label: Faithful servants, stewards, brothers, ministers, saints and witnesses; “Trustworthy is the saying”
rows.note: The same Greek adjective that is “faithful” of the Lord and “believing” of believers in the other rows; the gloss, not the Greek word, divides them, and the page does not say that “faithful” and “believing” are one meaning. Here it is a person's steadfast service, and the Pastoral formula “Trustworthy is the saying”.
rows._why: Panel fix (2026-10-10): these 35 verses (61% of the adjective's 67 verses with 'of little faith') had been dropped to 'More' in the consolidation, which left the adjective as God's attribute plus 'believers' only (rule 4: one sense presented as the whole). Restored in one row, not two, to stay near 26 rows: the persons (27: 'good and faithful servant', 1 Cor 4:2, Heb 3:5 Moses, Rev 2:10, 2:13) and the saying (1 Tim 1:15, 3:1, 4:9, 2 Tim 2:11, Titus 1:9, 3:8, Rev 21:5, 22:6) share a label that names both. 'Of little faith' stays under More (the noun row 'Faith with hearing, ... "little" and "great" faith' shows Matt 17:20).

rows.label: Called “believing”, “believers”
rows.note: The Greek is the same adjective that is “faithful” elsewhere in this list; the gloss, not the Greek word, divides them, and the page does not say that “believing” and “faithful” are one meaning.
rows._why: Panel: the noun and the verb are not stated to be the same; neither are the adjective's two glosses. The other uses of the adjective (faithful servants, stewards, brothers, ministers, saints, a witness, 27 verses; 'Trustworthy is the saying', 8; 'of little faith', 5) were rows of their own and are now under 'More'.
